package.title: 99 NAT-IE-Style Organic Chemistry MCQs with Explanations

questions.question: What is the usual valency of carbon in stable organic compounds?
Which general formula describes an acyclic alkane containing one saturated carbon chain?
Which formula is the general formula for an acyclic alkene with one carbon–carbon double bond?
Which formula is the general formula for an acyclic alkyne with one carbon–carbon triple bond?
What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in methane, CH₄?
What is the approximate H–C–H bond angle in ethene, C₂H₄?
What is the molecular formula of benzene?
Which compound is a saturated hydrocarbon?
Which functional group defines an alcohol?
Which functional group is present in an aldehyde?
Which functional group is characteristic of a ketone?
choices: A carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbon groups
A carbonyl carbon bonded to hydrogen
A hydroxyl group bonded to an aromatic ring

questions.question: Which group is the carboxyl group?
Which linkage is characteristic of an ester?
Which group is characteristic of an ether?
What is the simplest structure of a primary amine?
Which feature identifies a haloalkane?
choices: A halogen bonded to an alkyl carbon
An –OH group bonded to an alkyl carbon
A carbonyl group between two carbons

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₃?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂OH?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃COOH?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CHO?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₃?
What is the common IUPAC name of CH₃OCH₃?
How many structural isomers does C₄H₁₀ have?
Which pair consists of functional-group isomers with the formula C₂H₆O?
Which pair can exhibit cis–trans isomerism?
Which condition is necessary for a tetrahedral carbon to be a chiral centre?
choices: It is bonded to four identical groups
It is bonded to four different groups
It forms a double bond to oxygen

questions.question: What is the defining formula difference between successive members of a homologous series?
Which statement best describes structural isomers?
choices: They have the same molecular formula but different atom connectivity
They have different molecular formulas but identical connectivity
They differ only in the number of neutrons
They must have different functional groups

questions.question: Which intermolecular attraction is especially important between ethanol molecules?
Why does ethanol mix readily with water?
choices: It can form hydrogen bonds with water

questions.question: For a series of straight-chain alkanes, what generally happens to boiling point as chain length increases?
Which compound has the highest boiling point among these compounds with two carbon atoms?
What is the molar mass of ethanol, C₂H₆O, using C = 12, H = 1, and O = 16?
What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in ethanol, C₂H₆O, using molar mass 46 g mol⁻¹ and O = 16 g mol⁻¹?
What is the empirical formula of a compound with molecular formula C₂H₄?
What is the molecular formula of an alkane with five carbon atoms?
What is the formula of an acyclic monoalkene with five carbon atoms?
What is the formula of an acyclic monoalkyne with four carbon atoms?
How many sigma and pi bonds are present in one carbon–carbon double bond?
How many pi bonds are present in a carbon–carbon triple bond?
How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of propene?
What is the IUPAC name of HC≡CH?
What is the main organic product when ethene reacts completely with hydrogen in the presence of a suitable catalyst?
What visible change usually occurs when bromine water is shaken with an alkene under ordinary test conditions?
Under ultraviolet light, ethane reacts with chlorine mainly by which reaction type?
Which product forms when one mole of ethene undergoes addition of one mole of bromine?
Which polymer is formed by addition polymerization of ethene?
What is the monomer used to make poly(propene)?
Which small molecule is produced alongside an ester when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol?
Which pair of reactants can produce ethyl ethanoate and water?
What are the main organic products when an ester is hydrolysed with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
choices: A carboxylate salt and an alcohol

questions.question: What is the product of controlled oxidation of ethanol that stops at the aldehyde stage?
What is the usual oxidation product of propan-2-ol?
Which class of alcohol does not usually undergo oxidation with common laboratory oxidants without carbon–carbon bond cleavage?
What is the main organic product when ethanol is dehydrated under suitable hot, concentrated acid conditions?
Which observation is expected when an aldehyde gives a positive Tollens' test?
Which compound is expected to give a positive Tollens' test under standard conditions?
What is the usual result when a carboxylic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
What happens to blue litmus paper in a solution of ethanoic acid?
choices: It remains blue in every case

questions.question: What is produced by complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in excess oxygen?
Which dangerous gas can be produced by incomplete combustion of a carbon-containing fuel when oxygen is limited?
What is the carbon oxidation product when methane burns completely in oxygen?
In the reaction CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, how many moles of oxygen are needed for one mole of methane?
What is the main organic product of adding water to propene under acidic conditions, following the usual orientation rule?
What is the main product when propene reacts with hydrogen bromide in the absence of peroxides?
What reaction type occurs when hydrogen adds across a carbon–carbon double bond?
Which reagent is commonly used to oxidize a primary alcohol in an introductory laboratory reaction?
What colour change is commonly observed when acidified potassium dichromate(VI) is reduced during oxidation of an alcohol?
What is the usual name for the reaction in which an alkene is converted into an alkane by adding hydrogen?
What is the hybridization of each carbon atom in ethyne, HC≡CH?
What is the approximate bond angle around each carbon atom in ethyne?
Which structural feature makes benzene aromatic in the introductory model?
choices: A planar, cyclic, conjugated ring with delocalized pi electrons
A ring with only isolated single bonds
A chain with one carbon–carbon triple bond
A saturated ring containing only sp³ carbons

questions.question: Which reaction type is more characteristic of benzene than simple addition across its ring?
What is the usual catalyst for bromination of benzene in an introductory laboratory reaction?
What are the typical reagents for nitration of benzene?
choices: Concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulfuric acid

questions.question: What is the IUPAC retained name for benzene with one methyl substituent?
Which formula corresponds to methylbenzene?
In phenol, where is the hydroxyl group attached?
choices: Directly to an aromatic ring carbon
To a carbon one position away from the ring

questions.question: Why does benzene usually not decolourize bromine water in the same simple way as an alkene?
choices: Its aromatic ring is stabilized and does not undergo ordinary addition under those conditions
It reacts instantly with water to form an alcohol
It contains only carbon–carbon single bonds

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of cyclohexane?
How does the formula of a monocyclic cycloalkane with one ring compare with that of an acyclic alkane with the same number of carbons?
choices: It has two fewer hydrogen atoms
It has two more hydrogen atoms
It has the same number of hydrogen atoms
It has one fewer carbon atom

questions.question: Which structure is an example of a primary alcohol?
Which structure is a secondary alcohol?
Which structure is a tertiary alcohol?
Which is the correct name for CH₃CH₂CH₂OH when the –OH group is on the end carbon?
Which is the correct name for CH₃CH(OH)CH₃?
What is the name of the ester CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
Which two functional groups are present in an amino acid molecule in its basic introductory representation?
Which functional group defines a nitrile?
Which structure is an amide?
What is the main organic product when bromoethane reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide by substitution?
What is the main organic product when bromoethane is heated with ethanolic potassium hydroxide under elimination conditions?
Which functional group is present in propanal?
Which functional group is present in butanone?
Which product is expected when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
How many carbon atoms are present in one molecule of ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
What is the molecular formula of ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
Which statement about a catalyst in hydrogenation of an alkene is correct?
choices: It provides a surface that helps hydrogen add to the double bond
It becomes the main carbon-containing product
It changes the alkene into an alcohol by itself
It increases the number of carbon atoms in the product
